data.text:
# F1 and F3 closed, and the question the reviewer flagged as a trap, answered with the measurement

RED is record 76 and GREEN is record 77, 631 tests across the three classes. The RED's six failures were five
`AssertionError: HarnessError not raised`, the gate accepting what must be refused, including the fifth review's
scenario verbatim and its cleaner one-record variant, and one `ValueError: substring not found` where the
disclosure test looked for the shadow qualification inside the route clause and did not find it.

**The trap, and the answer.** The reviewer warned that comparing the green in every case is a bigger rule than
the one being repaired and would bite the case this ticket exists for, if a later round legitimately re-cites an
earlier round's red beside a corrected green. The implementer decided that case cannot arise and said so rather
than implying a distinction it was not making: a green re-run because the code moved belongs to a **later
attempt**, and `_require_the_pair_is_one_round` refuses that pair before the attribution is ever reached; inside
one attempt, a second green is one the accepted record of that attempt could have named and did not, written
while the checks were fresh and in the hash chain since. So the narrow repair and the general rule coincide, and
the general one is written.

**The measurement is what settled it rather than the argument**, which is how it should have been settled: over
every journal under `docs/harness/history/` plus SEEN-112's on its own branch, the narrow null-only repair moves
no recorded verdict and the general rule moves none either. No journal separates the two candidates, so the
narrower one would only be the same rule with a hole kept in it.

`_the_journal_pairs_it_with_another_check` now says, in both directions, that an accepted tdd record recorded this
pair differently, and it is silent on silence and on unanimous agreement. **The mirror at the green's end was
closed too, unprompted**, an accepted record naming another red for this green, because closing one end is
exactly what the previous round was returned for.

Three disclosures were corrected with it: `_the_journal_puts_it_elsewhere` now says it reads only the position,
which is the weaker half; `_require_the_pair_is_one_round`'s list is five rules with the fifth naming the same
paragraph's next omission; and `cited_check`'s statement of what a red is held to adds the round.

**F3 is the qualification put where the clause is made**: the route of the position an entry declares "refuses
nothing at all while `[routing] shadow` is true, because every route comparison returns before it compares in the
shadow window". The same qualification is on the route item in the pair rule's list. Nothing about the rule with
shadow off was weakened.

The three measurements: 294 citations in 107 pairs over every journal and SEEN-112's, with none cross-attempt,
none split across attempts, no red an accepted record puts at another slice and no pair an accepted record
recorded as another round. This ticket's own records 34 and 35 are still refused with the green as the failing
half, on the four files the later rounds rewrote, while red 34 is accepted on its green because record 39 pairs
34 with 35 and the new rule agrees with it. SEEN-112's five slice entries are unchanged and slice 3's pair stays
citable whole.

Two things noticed while measuring and left: within a single attempt, before any accepted record exists, the
pairing of a red to a green still rests on the citing record's word and nothing in the journal can corroborate
it; and `_positions_declared_for` normalises a malformed position to null, so a record carrying a non-integer
position reads as a null declaration rather than as a defect.
